metadata.title: Getting Started
metadata.description: Learn how to install Capacitor+ as a drop-in replacement for official Capacitor packages.

blocks.text: You can use our AI-Assisted Setup to install Capacitor+. Add the Capgo skills to your AI tool using the following command:
Use the `capacitor-plugins` skill from `Cap-go/capgo-skills` to install the `@capacitor-plus/core`, `@capacitor-plus/cli`, `@capacitor-plus/android`, and `@capacitor-plus/ios` packages in my project.
If you prefer Manual Setup, install the packages by running the following commands and follow the platform-specific instructions below:

npm install @capacitor-plus/android  # for Android
npm install @capacitor-plus/ios      # for iOS
If you have an existing Capacitor project, migrating to Capacitor+ is simple:

npm install @capacitor-plus/core @capacitor-plus/cli
npm install @capacitor-plus/android  # if using Android
npm install @capacitor-plus/ios      # if using iOS
No code changes required! Capacitor+ has the same API as official Capacitor. Your imports and code remain exactly the same.

Every upstream sync is analyzed for:
Command injection, XSS, path traversal, hardcoded secrets
Removed/renamed APIs, changed signatures, config changes
Null dereferences, unhandled exceptions, race conditions, memory leaks
Data loss scenarios, privacy violations, insecure storage
Obfuscated code, suspicious network calls, backdoors
If any issues are detected, the PR is flagged for manual review and will NOT be auto-merged. This ensures you always get stable, secure releases.
Have a PR stuck in the official Capacitor repo? Get it merged in Capacitor+:
The team will review, run CI, and merge if it passes
This way you and others can benefit from your work immediately without waiting for the upstream release cycle.
Yes. Capacitor+ is used in production apps. Every release passes the same test suite as official Capacitor, plus additional security analysis.

plugins work with Capacitor+ out of the box.
What if upstream releases a breaking change?
The AI security review flags breaking changes for manual review. You'll see the changes documented before they're merged.
